title: A word frequency tool
description:
A command-line tool that counts words in files or standard input, like a small `wc` and `sort | uniq -c` together.

```
$ words -n 5 essay.txt
  42 the
  21 of
  17 and
  12 to
   9 a
1,204 words, 386 different
```
hints: Read characters with `fgetc`, building each word in a growing buffer until a non-letter ends it (lessons 8.01 and 8.04).
At the end, copy the counts into an array and `qsort` it by count, then by word.
requirements: Options: `-n N` (how many to show), `-i` (ignore case), `--min=LEN` (skip shorter words), then files, or standard input when none.
Words counted in a hash table or a sorted array; any length of input and of words.
Errors (a missing file) to `stderr`, and a non-zero exit code when anything failed.
stretch: Make it handle UTF-8 letters such as `é` as part of words.
